text:
Darin: heads up — I'm proposing a short migration to prune low-value telemetry attributes from the console events table and unify the route identity hashing so dashboards don't break. need quick eyes on compatibility risks.
Sophia: can you sketch the core change? is this a column drop or move to a side-table?
Darin: plan is dual-write for 2w, read-adapter that maps old attributes -> new sparse attrs, then cutover. primary ops: (1) shrink `event_attrs` jsonb by removing developer-only keys, (2) add `route_hash_v2` that normalizes tenant+route metadata, (3) preserve old columns for read fallback.
Kevin: +1 on dual-write. curious about dashboard slowness during dual-write — we'll need to ensure index usage for route_hash_v2. what index do you recommend?
Darin: index suggestion: `CREATE INDEX ON console_events (route_hash_v2, timestamp DESC);` that'll keep p99 reads aligned with route queries. also TTL for pruned attrs to fall out of hot shards.
Mira: how are we detecting "low-value" attrs? we don't want to regress cost-based metrics in the console.
Darin: good question. using sampling + recent cardinality calc: run a query over 7d sample to compute unique counts per key, and remove keys with uniqueness > 100k AND < 0.1% usage in queries (console query logs). included sample SQL in the playbook:
```sql
-- sample attr pruning selector
WITH key_stats AS (
  SELECT attr_key, count(*) AS hits, approx_count_distinct(attr_value) AS distinct_vals
  FROM console_event_attr_samples
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
  GROUP BY attr_key
)
SELECT attr_key FROM key_stats WHERE hits < (SELECT percentile_cont(0.001) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY hits) FROM key_stats)
  OR distinct_vals > 100000;
```
Sophia: would prefer an explicit allowlist for metrics we know the dashboards use (sessions, errors, route_id). can we maintain an allowlist + auto-prune for everything else?
Darin: yes — default is allowlist + auto-prune. allowlist lives in config repo and syncs to ingest service at rollout time.
Ben: what about quota calc? route identity changes could affect per-route quotas and billing. Need to ensure billing uses stable identity during migration.
Darin: billing will continue to use route_key_v1 until we've validated parity in a verification window. flow: dual-write route_key_v2 -> gather mapping table, run matching, if >99.95% stable for 24h then switch billing read-source. fallback never removes v1 until billing cutover.
Kevin: can we add a small background job that emits mismatch stats by tenant so we can triage earlier?
Darin: already on the checklist: `route_identity_audit` job that writes daily mismatch rate to `ingest-metrics` and alerts if >0.05%.
Mira: on read adapter: is the adapter going to materialize denormalized columns for dashboard queries or translate queries on the fly?
Darin: translate on the fly for the initial window to avoid heavy backfills. we have a plan to materialize hot paths after 2w if p99s degrade. adapter pseudocode: 
````
if query references route_id then
  rewrite route_id -> coalesce(route_id_v1, route_id_v2_norm)
end
````
Sophia: UX for rollouts — product asks that dashboards should show a banner when we're in migration mode. can we expose migration state via the console API so frontend can show a tooltip?
Darin: yes, we'll add `/api/internal/migrations/console-attr-prune` that returns state and ETA. frontend will fetch and show banner for admins.
ingest-bot: deploy scheduled: dual-write ingest patch will be deployed to canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC.
Ben: safety guardrails — require a manual approval when mismatch rate >0.01% for any enterprise tenant. put an auto-block in the deploy pipeline.
Darin: added approval gate in the runbook section. also added a kill-switch HTTP endpoint to stop v2 writes.
Kevin: load-testing: have we simulated the extra io from dual-write and read-adapter? might need to bump write throughput on dedicated clusters.
Darin: yes, perf sim shows ~7% extra write QPS. Eng-infra recommends throttling dual-write replicas to 80% capacity and enabling burst autoscale for 3h after cutover.
Mira: what about analytics backfills? we might need to re-run some aggregation jobs that depend on pruned attrs.
Darin: backfills: small aggregate jobs will be run in shadow using v2 and compared. heavy backfills will be scheduled during low-traffic windows; playbook contains a backfill checklist and cost estimate.
Sophia: can we get the migration doc in GH so PMs and data-science can review the allowlist before we flip?
Darin: yep, I pushed the draft to https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-migrations/pull/42 — comments welcome.
Ben: final ask — add a dashboard that shows: (a) attr pruning candidates, (b) route identity mismatch by tenant, (c) p99 dashboard render latency. that'll make go/no-go easier.
Darin: noted, I'll add the grafana dashboard panel IDs to the runbook.
Kevin: 👍 schedule a canary postmortem after canary window so we capture any surprises.
Darin: will do. thanks folks — next step: review GH doc and I'll post the runbook link in #eng-sre once canary is live. :party_parrot:
